text:
Bob (Acme): Hi — after last night's cert rotation a subset of our clients (embedded devices) started failing TLS with 'certificate verify failed'. Browsers and curl from my laptop are fine.
Jane S.: Thanks, Bob. Are you seeing 502s at our gateway or client handshake failures? Any logs?
Bob (Acme): On our side the device logs show: 'TLS handshake failed: certificate has expired'. We confirmed by running openssl on a failing device (old OpenSSL 1.0.2). Paste below.
Bob (Acme): ```
$ openssl s_client -connect svc.acme.internal:443 -servername svc.acme.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Old Root CA, CN = Old Root
verify error:num=10:certificate has expired
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=svc.acme.internal
 1 s:/CN=Expired Intermediate
    i:/CN=Old Root
 2 s:/CN=New Intermediate
    i:/CN=New Root
---
```
Jane S.: Huh. So the device is selecting the expired intermediate from the chain returned by our endpoint. Browser sees a different path and succeeds.
Tom R.: Eng here. This is consistent with AIA/chain selection behavior: if the endpoint serves both the expired intermediate and the new intermediate in the bundle, older OpenSSL variants may pick the wrong intermediate (the expired one) during path building. That results in verification failure even though a valid path exists.
Jane S.: @Anna L. can you check what the rotation uploaded? rotator-bot should have logs.
rotator-bot: rotation job 2024-11-24T03:12:08Z completed for customer acme-private (bundle size: 3 certs). object://certs/acme-private/latest.pem uploaded sha256:def456...
Anna L.: I pulled the bundle from our object store — it contains leaf + expired-intermediate.pem + new-intermediate.pem + root.pem (the UI concatenated both intermediates). That explains the mixed selection.
Tom R.: Action: remove the expired intermediate from the served chain. For Private deployments we need to re-upload a sanitized chain: leaf -> new-intermediate -> root. Then trigger rotation.
Anna L.: I'll do that now. Steps I'm running:
```
# build sanitized bundle
cat leaf.pem new-intermediate.pem root.pem > sanitized-bundle.pem
# upload to object storage used by rotator
aws s3 cp sanitized-bundle.pem s3://private-rotations/acme-private/next.pem --profile infra-ops
# trigger rotation job
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/rotator/rotate -d '{"customer":"acme-private","bundle":"next.pem"}'
```
Jane S.: Bob, quick ask — can you confirm the devices have not pinned the expired intermediate explicitly? If they've pinned an intermediate the fix will need a device update.
Bob (Acme): They do not pin the intermediate; they only have the old root in the trust store. They relied on the server to provide intermediates.
Tom R.: OK good. That means removing the expired intermediate from the served chain should fix the device path-building. For verification run on a failing device (or an emulator) after rotation:
```
openssl s_client -connect svc.acme.internal:443 -servername svc.acme.internal -showcerts
# ensure chain order is leaf -> new-int -> root
# or verify explicitly:
openssl verify -CAfile <root.pem> -untrusted <new-intermediate.pem> leaf.pem
```
Anna L.: Rotation triggered and completed (rotator-bot confirmed). New bundle now contains only leaf + new-intermediate + root. rotator-bot: rotation job 2024-11-24T03:18:12Z completed for customer acme-private (bundle size: 3 certs) sha256:ghi789...
Bob (Acme): Re-tested on device — TLS handshake now succeeds. No more verify errors. Thanks! :tada:
Jane S.: Great. Follow-ups:
- We should update the UI/validation to warn if an uploaded bundle contains multiple intermediates with overlapping chains.
- Add a rotator check to warn when a bundle contains an expired certificate.
Tom R.: Agreed. I'll file a small infra ticket to add server-side validation and a rotator precheck.
Anna L.: Ticket created: INF-2982 "rotator: validate bundle for expired/duplicate intermediates". I'll add a link to the customer's rotation objects.
Bob (Acme): All good from our side — closing.
Jane S.: Closing the support thread. If anything else pops up ping me or @eng. :thumbsup:
